newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Thousands attend funeral in Belgium of dead child.
newsitem.headline: Thousands attend funeral in Belgium of dead child.

text.p: Thousands of people from all walks of life turned out in central Brussels on Saturday to pay their last respects to a young girl found dead in a garage basement -- the fifth such grisly discovery in six months.

Police estimated that at least 15,000 people were gathered around the Islamic Centre in the city's Cinquentenaire park with hundreds more inside as the memorial service began for Loubna Benaissa, aged nine when she disappeared in August 1992.
The body of Loubna, who disappeared while shopping for her mother, was discovered on Wednesday in a steel trunk in the basement of a garage in the Brussels suburb of Ixelles where she lived.
Patrick Derochette, a convicted violent child molester who worked at the garage, has been charged with abduction, rape of a child under 10 and illegal imprisonment leading to death.
Yves Crochelet, a psychiatrist who studied Derochette in 1984 when he was given a suspended sentence, described him on Friday as a "psychopathic pervert".

A representative of King Albert attended the funeral, as did representatives of the government, the parents of the four other young girls who have been found dead since August and those of other children who are still missing.

"You are very strong and I embrace you very strongly," Marie-Noel Bouzet, the mother of Elizabeth Brichet who has been missing since December 1989, told the congregation in a voice breaking with emotion speaking directly to Loubna's parents.
Outside in the packed park the atmosphere was calm but sad.

"It is really sadness that is at the forefront today," teacher Mohammed Fassi , a friend of the Benaissa family, told Reuters as he stood with his two young daughters watching a giant screen relaying the televised service.
"It is important for them to be here," he said referring to his daughters. "I want them to be witnesses."
Nearby a small shrine to Loubna was covered with flowers, childrens' drawings and messages of sorrow and support.

Loubna's remains will be flown later on Saturday to the family's home town of Tangiers for burial on Sunday. It will be accompanied by the family as well as some of the parents of the dead and missing children and representatives of the government.
Shock at the discovery of Loubna's body has turned to anger at the evident bungling by Brussels police in the first investigation into Loubna's dissappearance.
Prime Minister Jean-Luc Dehaene admitted on Friday that mistakes had been made.
"We cannot fail to take note of the fact that the Brussels inquiry failed. The Justice Minister will take the necessary measures," he told reporters.
The discovery of Loubna's body brought to five the number of dead young girls found in Belgium since last August when another convicted paedophile, Marc Dutroux, was arrested.

Two young, sexually-abused girls were rescued from a dungeon in the basement of one of Dutroux' houses and the bodies of four girls were unearthed on two other properties either owned by or connected with him. Dutroux has been charged with murder.

There have been growing allegations of official protection for Dutroux, a theme that a special parliamentary commission has increasingly focused on since it began investigating bungled police investigations five months ago.
On Thursday the commission, which had been due to report on March 15, was given an extra month to pursue its inquiries.
Police have not established any links between Dutroux and Derochette.
